update.name: Funeral home
update.notes: photo from Mark, 771 N. Crafford St., 2010. Legacy.com says this funeral home has been locally owned and operated since 1942, at 771 N. Crafford St. The 1950 stop is the first stop after 1942, so the use changes here. The Martin-Hollis name is later, and it is not painted on. The house stays as drawn.

add.name: Mickelberry Food Products plant (operated by Ready Foods by 1965).
add.sourceMap: Cheryl Douglas, Community News Brief, 24 March 2026
add.notes: Mickelberry Food Production Company, believed to operate at the west end of Davis Street from 1940 to 1965, where Bushnell Tank stands today, near the tracks. The footprint is an estimate: a block long and half a block wide, 360 by 180 feet. Mostly one story. The 1944 Avon sheet was checked for a labeled plant and does not name this works. The main block burned on 26 February 1965. A Macomb Daily Journal line quoted in the article is dated 1964; the article's own date is 1965, and 1965 is used.

add.name: Mickelberry offices
add.sourceMap: Cheryl Douglas, Community News Brief, 24 March 2026
add.notes: The two-story section of the Mickelberry plant, offices and upstairs storage, on the main block. It burned with the plant on 26 February 1965.

add.name: Mickelberry north addition
add.sourceMap: McDonough Democrat, 9 November 1944, quoted by Cheryl Douglas
add.notes: Large addition to the north of the Mickelberry building, completed by 9 November 1944, for sausage machines and canning. The size is an estimate. It burned with the plant on 26 February 1965. The model has no stop between 1920 and 1950, so this wing is first drawn at the 1950 stop, with the 1940 main block.

add.name: Mickelberry cold storage
add.sourceMap: Cheryl Douglas, Community News Brief, 24 March 2026
add.notes: Cold storage at the west end of the Mickelberry plant. The fire account says this room was not damaged on 26 February 1965. It is kept for 1965 through 1969 and is not carried into 1970, because no source says it was still standing then.

add.name: Mickelberry shed
add.sourceMap: Cheryl Douglas, Community News Brief, 24 March 2026
add.notes: Small shed just west of the Mickelberry plant. It escaped the 26 February 1965 fire. Kept for 1965 through 1969 only.
